sections.label: Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act amendments
sections.summary: The Bill proposes amendments to the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act, passed in 1990 and effective in 1992.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This Bill proposes amendments to the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act (MRHA).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: MRHA was passed in 1990 and came into effect in 1992.

sections.label: MRHA key features
sections.summary: The MRHA covered conduct harming religious tolerance, let the Minister issue restraining orders, and set up a Presidential Council for Religious Harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The MRHA was passed and had these key features: one, it covered conduct that harmed religious tolerance; two, there were powers for the Minister to issue orders restraining harmful conduct; and three, a Presidential Council for Religious Harmony (PCRH) was set up, which could consider these orders.

sections.label: Global religious trends and challenges
sections.summary: It cites growing religiosity, identity politics, religion-related violence, the Internet and social media, and foreign interference, projecting 87% religiously-affiliated by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: First, growing religiosity and increased reliance on identity politics around the world; second, increased violence committed in the name of religion; third, the Internet and social media; and fourth, increased possibilities for interference by countries in the affairs of other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If Members look at the 2015 Pew Research Centre survey, it is projected that by 2050, 87% of the world's population will be religiously-affiliated.

sections.label: Religious organisations affirm Commitment
sections.summary: Earlier this year, more than 300 religious organisations affirmed the Commitment to Safeguard Religious Harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, more than 300 religious organisations affirmed the Commitment to Safeguard Religious Harmony.

sections.label: Singapore religious diversity and harmony studies
sections.summary: Studies found Singapore the most religiously diverse country, first of 140 for ethnic minority tolerance, and inter-religious harmony improving.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If we go back to a Pew Research Centre study in 2014 on religious diversity, it showed that Singapore was the most religiously diverse country in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Yet, a 2016 Gallup World Poll ranked us first out of 140 countries for tolerance of ethnic minorities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: A 2019 Institute of Policy Studies and OnePeople.sg joint study also found inter-religious harmony in Singapore improving.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Nine in 10 said the level of racial and religious harmony in Singapore is moderate, high or very high.

sections.label: Moving religion offences to MRHA
sections.summary: The MRHA is updated to move religion-related Penal Code offences into it, making it an offence to knowingly urge religiously grounded violence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: You want to allow for those religious influences but at the same time do not want them to affect us negatively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We are updating the MRHA to deal with some of the challenges that I have spoken about.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: First, we are moving over the religion-related offences from the Penal Code and housing them under the MRHA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The amendments will make it an offence to knowingly urge violence, on the ground of religion or religious belief, against any person or group.

sections.label: Foreign donations disclosure requirements
sections.summary: The Bill requires religious organisations to disclose foreign donations and affiliations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces requirements on religious organisations to disclose foreign donations and affiliations.

sections.label: Amending Order immediate effect
sections.summary: Because the Internet and social media make 14 days too long, the Order will be amended to take immediate effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: With the Internet and social media, 14 days is too long.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, we will amend for the Order to take immediate effect.

sections.label: Five changes to religious laws
sections.summary: The passage lists five changes: foreign influence safeguards, updating the RO, introducing the CRI, porting religion-related Penal Code provisions to MRHA, and related Penal Code amendments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, introduction of safeguards against foreign influence that affect religious harmony; second the updating of the RO; third, introduction of the CRI; fourth, porting over of religion-related provisions from the Penal Code to MRHA; and fifth, related amendments to the Penal Code.

sections.label: Disclosing foreign donations of S$10,000
sections.summary: After discussions with apex religious organisations, religious groups must disclose single foreign donations of S$10,000 or more.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: These baseline safeguards were developed after extensive discussions with apex religious organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will require religious groups to disclose single foreign donations that are S$10,000 or more.

sections.label: Exemptions and office-holder citizenship
sections.summary: The Minister can exempt other donation types via subsidiary legislation, and the President, Secretary and Treasurer must be a Singapore Citizen or PR.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Minister will be able to set out other types of donations that can be exempted from disclosure requirements through subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We will require the President, Secretary and Treasurer of the religious group to be either a Singapore Citizen or PR.

sections.label: Executive committee citizenship majority
sections.summary: The majority of the religious group's executive committee or governing body must be Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In addition to this, the majority of the executive committee or governing body of the religious group must be Singapore Citizens.

sections.label: Definition of foreign affiliation
sections.summary: New section 16B defines foreign affiliation as an arrangement where a religious group follows a foreign principal's instructions or is substantially controlled by it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Foreign affiliation is defined in the new section 16B as an arrangement with a foreign principal where the religious group is accustomed to act in accordance with its instructions, or where the foreign principal exercises total or substantial control over the religious group’s activities.

sections.label: Restriction orders against religious groups
sections.summary: Clause 5 allows an RO against a religious group to counter foreign influence threatening religious tolerance and public order, imposing donation and office-holding safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Under the new clause 5, an RO can be issued against a religious group to pre-empt, prevent or reduce any foreign influence affecting the religious group which may undermine religious tolerance among different religious groups in Singapore, and present a threat to public peace and public order in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The RO can impose additional safeguards on religious groups: (a) to prohibit or restrict receiving of anonymous donations, or of foreign donations by the religious group; (b) to ensure that every member of the governing body is a citizen of Singapore or prohibit a specific foreigner or PR from holding office in the governing body in the religious group.

sections.label: Removal of 14-day notice
sections.summary: The 14-day notice period for issuing ROs is removed, so ROs take immediate effect.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, we will remove the 14-day notice period for the issuance of ROs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The RO will now be issued and take immediate effect.

sections.label: Community remedial initiative offer
sections.summary: The CRI is offered by the Minister to an alleged offender, setting out remedial actions to mend ties with the aggrieved community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The CRI is offered by the Minister to an alleged offender which will set out the remedial actions that can be taken to mend ties with the aggrieved community.

sections.label: Maximum punishment for offence
sections.summary: Because force or violence is likely to occur, the offence carries a maximum of 10 years' imprisonment, or fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Because of the seriousness of the outcome, that force or violence is likely to occur, any person who commits this offence will be subjected to the maximum punishment of 10 years’ imprisonment, or fine, or both.

sections.label: Coverage of private religious speech
sections.summary: This covers religious leaders speaking with close family or close friends, with extraterritorial coverage for offences committed overseas targeting Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This would cover situations where the religious leader is speaking with close family members in their household, or a small group of very close friends in his house.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: There will be extraterritorial coverage for these offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: If the offence is committed overseas, targets Singapore and has an impact in Singapore, this will be covered.

sections.label: Penal Code section 74 scope
sections.summary: Section 74's scope expands to all Penal Code offences and maximum punishments increase from one-and-a-half to two times, except death or life imprisonment offences.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: First, the scope of section 74 will be expanded to cover all offences in the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Second, the enhancement of maximum punishments will be increased from one-and-a-half to two times, except those which are punishable with death or imprisonment for life.

sections.label: Egypt churches protested and shut
sections.summary: In Egypt from October 2017 to October 2018, 15 churches were violently protested against by Muslims and 11 were shut.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In Egypt, over a span of 13 months from October 2017 to October 2018, 15 churches were violently protested against by Muslims and 11 had to be shut.

sections.label: Sri Lanka Christians discrimination incidents
sections.summary: In 2018 Sri Lanka had 86 verifiable cases of discrimination, threats and violence against Christians, and 26 such incidents occurred this year before the Easter bombings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2018, there were 86 verifiable cases of discrimination, threats and violence against Christians in Sri Lanka and 26 such incidents occurred this year, before the Easter bombings, including the disruption of a Sunday service.

sections.label: Amending law for religious harmony
sections.summary: The law needs amending especially to address the swiftness with which messages of violence and hatred can spread.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Some may question the need to amend the law because it seems to have been efficacious in preserving religious harmony which we still enjoy today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But my own view is that the law needs to be amended, especially to address the swiftness with which messages of violence and hatred can spread.

sections.label: ROs go through PCRH
sections.summary: ROs and extensions of ROs have to go through the PCRH per sections 11 and 13 to address concerns of abuse of power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To address concerns of abuse of power, RO and extensions of ROs have to go through the PCRH per sections 11 and 13.

sections.label: Section 17F duties gradated
sections.summary: The duties undergirding the offences in the new section 17F are gradated based on whether or not the person is a religious leader.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The duties undergirding the offences in the new section 17F are gradated based on whether or not the person is a religious leader.

sections.label: Definition of religious leader
sections.summary: A speaker asks the Minister to explain the definition of "religious leader", noting volunteers still serve well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These people still do great service as volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Therefore, it would be helpful if the Minister could explain the definition of "religious leader".

sections.label: Rules for corporatised religious groups
sections.summary: A question asks whether the same requirements on Singaporeans and foreign persons apply to corporatised religious charitable groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Do the same requirements relating to Singaporeans and foreign persons apply to corporatised religious charitable groups?

sections.label: Foreign persons limits flexibility
sections.summary: A question asks how flexible the law is and how limits on foreign persons can avoid burdening institutions, orders and missionaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Considering the long-standing contribution and ties that Singapore's religious groups have with overseas religious groups, how flexible and nimble enough is our law to ensure that the intent of this Bill is achieved without reducing the good work of institutions here?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: How can we ensure that the limitations on foreign persons will not be overly onerous in institutions, orders and missionaries who continue to do sterling work in Singapore?

sections.label: Updating religious harmony legislation
sections.summary: A speaker supports the Bill, saying the Government has not invoked the existing law in 27 years and now needs to update it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Being able to come together to contribute to a meaningful cause testifies to the precious religious harmony we enjoy in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill is part of that work, that constant work in progress and, therefore, and I support it.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Since its passage, the Government has not had to invoke the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Now, 27 years later, observing a different environment, the Government has identified the need to update and improve this piece of legislation.

sections.label: Concerns on new section 17F
sections.summary: A speaker raises concerns about new section 17F, which restrains creating ill-will, with an offence when public peace is threatened.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The new section 17F raises several concerns to me.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The provisions are meant to curb and restrain any attempt at creating ill-will and feelings of hatred towards other religious groups by either a religious leader or an individual who is not a religious leader.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But for the latter, it is an offence when the action is deemed to “threaten the public peace or order in Singapore or any part of Singapore”.

sections.label: Ambiguity of wounded and public order
sections.summary: A speaker worries that ambiguity over being wounded and threatened public order can escalate and expand conflicts.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: My concern is that the ambiguities of what being wounded constitutes and, when public order or peace is threatened, can lead to some claims of ill-will that lead to an unintended escalation and expansion of the conflicts.

sections.label: Live and let live attitude
sections.summary: The passage urges a live-and-let-live attitude while welcoming the Bill's force against those seeking to divide the community or any faith community.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We must respect and adopt an attitude of live and let live towards one another, while feeling equally attached to our faith and our desire to do good.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But I would welcome the force of this Bill to be applied to those seeking to divide the community or, for that matter, any faith community.

sections.label: Secularism barriers in public life
sections.summary: The passage states that if compartmentalisation is impossible, barriers of secularism in public life must be guarded, strengthening common spaces so religious actors cannot impose their will on public policy.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, if we agree that if it is not possible to compartmentalise ourselves, then we must be alert to the breaching of the barriers of secularism in our public life.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: That is, we must continue to strengthen our common spaces and ensure that religious actors cannot impose their will on public policy to the detriment of other religious groups or the public good.

sections.label: Measures against egregious cases
sections.summary: The passage says strong measures are clear-cut for threats, open harassment and incitement to violence, but community service work or engagement with community groups is more appropriate where dialogue is possible.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The need for strong and decisive measures against egregious cases – threats, open harassment and incitement to violence – are clear-cut.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Yet, where engagement and dialogue are possible, the imposition of community service work or engagement with community groups would be more appropriate.

sections.label: Law as last resort
sections.summary: The passage states that the use of the law is the last resort.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In fact, the use of the law is the last resort.

sections.label: Sensitivity in ambiguous cases
sections.summary: The passage urges the Government to exercise sensitivity where there is ambiguity on both the alleged culprit and alleged victim, while agreeing on a legal response to clear-cut egregious cases.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While no one can disagree with the need to use a legal response to clear-cut egregious cases, I would urge the Government to exercise sensitivity in cases where there is some ambiguity on both the alleged culprit and alleged victim.

sections.label: MRHA since 1992
sections.summary: The passage states that since coming into effect in 1992, MRHA has been a critical complement to Singapore's work on strengthening religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Since coming into effect in 1992, MRHA has been a critical complement to Singapore’s work on strengthening religious harmony.

sections.label: Amending Act against polarising forces
sections.summary: The world faces greater risk of polarising forces, so the Act is being amended to keep serving its original intent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The world is at far more risk of polarising forces that divide rather than unite people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: It is timely that we amend the Act to ensure that it continues to serve its original intent, today.

sections.label: Leaders support proposed amendments
sections.summary: Respected leaders have raised concerns on race and religion and strongly support the proposed amendments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: These respected leaders, and many more in Singapore, have expressed similar concerns when we discuss issues of race and religion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: They understand the importance and urgency of dealing with the risks unequivocally and they have expressed strong support for the proposed amendments.

sections.label: Interracial and inter-religious trust
sections.summary: People help one another, do business and attend life events, and surveys show interracial and inter-religious trust is high and rising.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We offer help to one another, do business together, and attend one another’s life events, such as weddings and funerals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This approach has served us well and survey results show both interracial and inter-religious trust is high and rising.

sections.label: Goodwill committees to IRCCs
sections.summary: Goodwill committees formed after the 1964 riots were the foundation for the IRCCs formalised in 2002.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: When faced with the communal riots in 1964, we established goodwill committees comprising racially diverse community leaders to calm the situation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This was the foundation for the Inter-Racial and Religious Confidence Circles (IRCCs) which was formalised in 2002 to foster community bonding at the local level.

sections.label: Religious harmony declarations and commitment
sections.summary: An IRHC launched the Declaration on Religious Harmony in 2003, and in 2019 leaders launched the Commitment to Safeguard Religious Harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: An Inter-Religious Harmony Circle (IRHC) comprising religious leaders and Government representatives, developed and launched the Declaration on Religious Harmony in 2003.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In June 2019, our religious leaders launched the Commitment to Safeguard Religious Harmony that affirms the shared values to safeguard our religious harmony and the norms of social interaction across religions to foster a cohesive society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: More than 300 religious organisations have since affirmed the Commitment.

sections.label: Interfaith prayers and Harmony Fund
sections.summary: Religious leaders of different faiths pray together at events, and Singaporeans are encouraged to use MCCY's Harmony Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The sight of 10 religious leaders representing different faiths, conducting prayers side-by-side, simultaneously and jointly, would be familiar to Singaporeans who have been to, for instance, Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) Officer Cadet Course commissioning parades, the World War II commemorative ceremonies, or watched their pre-race blessing of the Formula One races.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We want to tap on the collective wisdom and ideas of Singaporeans and encourage the community to leverage the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth's (MCCY’s) Harmony Fund to continue developing innovative projects that promote racial and religious harmony.

sections.label: IBM cultural adaptability programme
sections.summary: IBM runs a Cultural Adaptability Programme using workshops and resources to raise employee awareness of different beliefs and practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For instance, IBM has a Cultural Adaptability Programme to enhance the level of awareness and appreciation on different beliefs and practices among their employees through structured workshops and resources.

sections.label: Bill updates preventive regime
sections.summary: The Bill updates a preventive regime that gives the Cabinet executive authority to keep religion out of politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill updates what is essentially a preventive regime, albeit one that gives the Cabinet executive authority to endeavour that religion is kept out of politics.

sections.label: Workers' Party on religious harmony
sections.summary: The Workers' Party does not object to the Bill's amendments, citing regional environment, social mores and social media as concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To that end, the Workers' Party does not find the amendments mooted in the Bill before the House objectionable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, the confluence of the regional environment, social mores and the ubiquity of social media are perhaps of equal, if not more, concern in the maintenance of religious harmony than in the 1980s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Only last week, a Malay civil rights group openly called for a Vote Muslim First campaign with regard to the upcoming by-election for Tanjung Piai in Johor.

sections.label: Religious leaders inviting politicians
sections.summary: Invitations by religious leaders and organisations to politicians, especially near elections, would signal the religious laity to support that politician.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, the imprudent timing of invitations by religious leaders and organisations to politicians, particularly in the run-in to elections, would inevitably have a signaling effect on the religious laity of any faith to support the politician in question.

sections.label: Removal of Executive power check
sections.summary: The Bill removes the 14-day notice to the Council on impending ROs, and the Workers' Party supports the amendments despite concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One important change is the removal of a check on Executive power.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Act today, a 14-day notice period operates to inform PCRH about the impending issuance of an RO.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the Bill before the House today, the Government seeks to remove any requirement to notify the Council, ostensibly because it seeks to move quickly against an offender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I wish to clarify with the Minister, in the event a religious leader is slapped with an RO to remove an offending post from his or her Facebook page, for example, and he or she does not do so, what recourse, legislation or regulations will the Government turn to, to see that the offending statement or statements is/are speedily removed, particularly if it cannot be classified as a false statement of fact?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A multiracial and multi-religious Singapore and the way our people accommodate differences and diverse views and display a genuine tolerance towards one another are a key strength of this country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Workers' Party supports these amendments, notwithstanding our concerns about the application of the underlying Act.

sections.label: Offences for religious violence incitement
sections.summary: Urging religious violence carries up to 10 years' imprisonment or a fine, or both; inciting hostility or insulting religion carries up to five years or a fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Under the framework of offences, any individual who urges violence against any person or group on the basis of religion or violence against any religious group or member faces imprisonment of up to 10 years or a fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A religious leader or anyone posing a risk of disturbing public peace who incites hostility against a religion, insults someone's religion or wounds their religious feelings face imprisonment of up to five years or a fine, or both.

sections.label: Community Remedial Initiative introduction
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Community Remedial Initiative, where offenders make amendments to offended parties and understand their wrongs in a multiracial society.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On this note, I am glad to see the introduction of the Community Remedial Initiative (CRI), where offenders will be asked to make amendments to offended parties and be given opportunities to understand how they did wrong in the context of a multiracial society.

sections.label: Bill requires Singaporean key appointment holders
sections.summary: The Bill aims to deter this by requiring key appointment holders or equivalent to be Singaporeans or PRs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill aims to deter this by requiring key appointment holders or equivalent to be Singaporeans or PRs.

sections.label: Religious group key appointment holders
sections.summary: Key appointment holders of religious groups must be Singaporeans or PRs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Key appointment holders of religious groups must be Singaporeans or PRs.

sections.label: Religious leaders, 377A, social harmony
sections.summary: The speaker notes religious leaders opposed repealing section 377A, stigmatised some groups, and asks the Ministry to also protect social harmony.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In recent years, some religious leaders here have established clear positions against the repeal of section 377A of the Penal Code and have thrown their moral weight behind this.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Some have also stigmatised those whose personal lives do not conform to religious precepts, including single parents and persons of different sexual orientations.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is true that several mainstream religions do not accept these ways of life.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But a common view among some religions does not by itself justify the use of the pulpit to influence public policy.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Nor does it mean that these acts from the pulpit have no consequences; they harm the feelings of those they condemn, and they create real risks of discrimination or violence against these minority groups.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thus, while the primary aim of MRHA must be to protect religious harmony, I ask the Ministry to also have regard to protecting social harmony.

sections.label: MRHA success not invoked
sections.summary: It is often said that MRHA's mark of success is that it has not been invoked since being codified almost 30 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: When we speak of MRHA, it is oft said that its mark of success for this legislation is the fact that it has not been invoked since it was first codified into law almost 30 years ago.

sections.label: Asking for update on concerns
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Ministry can update the House on other concerns, such as those in the previous ISD report, that accelerated the need to amend the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: At this point, I would like to ask if the Ministry would be able to update the House that besides the reasons already publicly raised by a number of political officeholders for updating of the Act, are there any other concerns, such as those raised in the previous ISD report that have also accelerated the need to amend the Act at this point in time.

sections.label: MHA engagement with religious organisations
sections.summary: The speaker requests MHA to engage more publicly with religious organisations and help disseminate what the Act's amendments mean for religious practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On this front, my next request is for MHA to engage more publicly with religious organisations and assist in the information dissemination process of what the amendments of the Act itself would mean or not mean for the practice of religion.

sections.label: Minister issuing ROs immediately
sections.summary: Amendments to section 8(4), (5) and (6) let the Minister issue an RO directly and immediately instead of 14 days later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In the amendments to section 8(4), (5) and (6), the Minister can now directly and immediately issue an RO rather than the 14 days later stipulated under the current section 8(6).

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Speed is of the essence and, as seen in the Christchurch massacre and also in the recent Sri Lankan Buddhist-Muslim clashes, having the ability to shut down hate speech to viral is paramount.

sections.label: Concerns of consulted religious leaders
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to share concerns or objections raised by consulted religious leaders and how they were addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Can I ask that the Minister share with the House what were the concerns, if any, and perhaps even objections that were raised by religious leaders who were consulted, and how those concerns were appropriately addressed?

sections.label: CRI effectiveness and circumstances
sections.summary: The speaker asks under what circumstances a CRI would be effective, for examples in other jurisdictions, and whether an independently initiated CRI counts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Under what circumstances would a CRI be effective and are there examples in other jurisdictions that have shown its effectiveness?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Also, if the Minister does not issue a CRI, but one is undertaken independently at the initiative of both the offender and the aggrieved, will this be taken into consideration?

sections.label: Religious organisations meeting requirement
sections.summary: According to the Ministry, about 100 of around 2,500 religious organisations here will not meet the proposed Bill's requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In addition, according to the Ministry, the proposed Bill would mean that out of around 2,500 religious organisations here today, about 100 will not be able to meet this requirement.

sections.label: Impact on Article 15 freedom
sections.summary: The speaker asks how this would impact the constitutional guarantee of freedom of religion under Article 15 of the Constitution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How would this be of impact to the constitutional guarantee of freedom of religion under Article 15 of the Constitution?

sections.label: Religious groups foreign affiliations Bill
sections.summary: The Bill imposes reporting on religious groups' foreign affiliations and donations, lets the Minister remove foreigners from governing bodies, while Article 15(3) protects religious self-management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill imposes reporting requirements on religious groups regarding their foreign affiliations and donations and may require certain donations from foreign principals to be returned or surrendered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill also empowers the Minister to require the removal of foreigners from the governing bodies of religious institutions if such persons are deemed by the Government to have priorities that are inappropriate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, Article 15(3) of the Constitution provides that every religious group has the right to manage its own religious affairs.

sections.label: Religious leader election exhortation
sections.summary: It asks whether a religious leader should exhort his congregation during a General Election to "Vote for Stability".

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Is it appropriate for a religious leader to exhort his congregation during a General Election to “Vote for Stability”?

sections.label: Religious leaders polarising society
sections.summary: It warns religious leaders could polarise society, questions how an RO could contradict written law, and notes the Workers' Party shares the Government's concern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If unchecked, there is a possibility that, over time, there would be a polarisation of society along political lines, caused not by foreign influences, but by Singapore’s own religious leaders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Such a prospect could fracture social cohesion and divide society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This section states that an RO issued by the Minister has effect “despite the provisions of any other written law in force.” The explanatory note to the Bill touches on section 16F but is not clear as to how an RO could be contrary to a written law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Without clarification, the section reads as if an RO may breach other laws or be illegal in some manner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry explain what this is all about, please?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The then First Deputy Prime Minister Mr Goh Chok Tong told the House that the Cabinet had not been unanimous in deciding whether to legislate and decided to mull over it and consult widely for several years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When the Bill was presented, he said, “In a sense, this Bill is a recognition of a retrogression, or potential deterioration, in religious harmony.” Sir, the Workers’ Party shares this concern of the Government and is prepared to work with the Government on this aspect.

sections.label: Minister Shanmugam defining hate speech
sections.summary: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law defined hate speech as expression spreading, inciting, promoting or justifying hatred based on intolerance, and revulsion for it has two sources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In his Ministerial Statement on Restricting Hate Speech to Maintain Racial and Religious Harmony, the Minister for Home Affairs and Law Mr Shanmugam had defined hate speech as "all forms of expression which spread, incite, promote, or justify racial hatred, xenophobia or other forms of hatred based on intolerance." Our revulsion for hate speech stems from two sources.

sections.label: UN Secretary-General on hate speech
sections.summary: In February 2019, United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called hate speech a menace to democratic values, social stability and peace.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In February 2019, the United Nations Secretary-General Mr Antonio Guterres called hate speech a "menace to democratic values, social stability, peace".

sections.label: Masagos on external influences on Muslims
sections.summary: Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs Masagos Zulkifli said external influences have tried to reshape how Muslims live, including being exclusivist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In Singapore, our Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs, Mr Masagos Zulkifli, has said that there have been external influences trying to "reshape" how Muslims live their lives, including being "exclusivist".

sections.label: US and German speech laws
sections.summary: The US prohibits speech likely to lead to imminent lawless action, and the German Criminal Code criminalises incitement of hatred against or insult of a racial or religious group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In the US, speech is prohibited if it is likely to lead to "imminent lawless action".

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The German Criminal Code criminalises the incitement of hatred against, or insult of, a racial or religious group.

sections.label: Justifying more robust laws
sections.summary: From this principle, laws are justified in being made more robust amid rising strident views and online promulgation of what could not be said before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: From this principle, we are, therefore, justified in making our laws more robust, in a climate where strident views are rising, and much that cannot be said in the past, is now freely promulgated online.

sections.label: Support for MRHA amendments
sections.summary: A speaker supports the Bill, noting a risk of over-zealous application, and describes two principles: moderate religious practice and tolerance, and an offence for insulting religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: A second, perhaps more sustained argument could be that the amendments make the laws more robust, which runs the risk of over-zealous application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In short, Sir, I support this Bill because we, in this House, we cannot say something is important and, at the same time, we shirk from the hard work of regulating it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The two key principles of this Act are; first, that followers of religions in Singapore live their religious lives moderately, practise tolerance towards religious differences and do not do anything that can cause hatred and enmity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Briefly, what I understand from the Explanatory Note is that a person is deemed to have committed an offence if he willfully becomes involved in acts that insult a religion or the religious beliefs or the activities of others in Singapore, whereby those acts; one, cause hatred towards another religion; two, injure the feelings of followers of other religions; and three, will affect the law and public order.

sections.label: Preacher's motive and religion-politics separation
sections.summary: A preacher sharing Quran teachings would be deemed to have committed an offence under MRHA, and the second principle is that politics and religion should be separated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The preacher that I mentioned in my example will be deemed to have committed an offence under MRHA even though the preacher's real motive is to share the teachings that are found in the Quran.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second principle is that politics and religion should be separated.

sections.label: Oaths and religion in politics
sections.summary: Christian Members of Parliament can hold the Bible and say "So, help me God" in oaths, but using religion for political advantage is wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We can see during the ceremony that Members of Parliament who are Christians can hold the Bible when taking their oaths and they conclude their oaths with the phrase "So, help me God".

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, Sir, I agree that it is certainly wrong to use religion in order to gain political advantage.

sections.label: IPS and OnePeople.sg racial relations study
sections.summary: In Singapore's first study by the Institute of Policy Studies and OnePeople.sg on racial relations, four in 10 Singaporeans said they decide a person's behaviour and views based on race before interacting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: More than 50 years after our pledge was written, in Singapore's very first study by the Institute of Policy Studies and OnePeople.sg on the state of racial relations, four out of 10 Singaporeans said that they decide what a person's behaviour and views will be like based on their race even before they interact with them.

sections.label: Religious leader incitement defence
sections.summary: Section 17F lets a religious leader accused of inciting religious hatred defend himself by proving his message was meant only for a domestic gathering and he could not have anticipated wider reach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under section 17F, if a religious leader is accused of inciting religious hatred or ill-will, he would be able to defend himself by proving his message was meant only for a domestic gathering and that he could not have anticipated that it would reach unintended audiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Incitement, unlike insult, can cause serious harm even if the leader's words are heard only by a small circle.

sections.label: CRI participation limit question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the CRI should be limited in how many times individuals and organisations may participate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Should there be a limit to the CRI to not only individuals but also organisations on how many times they can participate in it?

sections.label: Survey on religious leaders inciting
sections.summary: 97.2% of those in this age group felt it was unacceptable or very unacceptable for religious leaders to incite violence or hatred against other religions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In addition, 97.2% of those in this age group felt that it was either unacceptable or very unacceptable for religious leaders to incite violence or hatred against other religions.

sections.label: Sections 17E offences scope
sections.summary: Sections 17E(1) and (2) make it an offence for any person to knowingly urge force or violence on religious grounds against a target distinguished by religion, ethnicity, descent, nationality, language, political opinion or other characteristic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It also expands the scope of protection beyond religious groups against such intolerance and discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I especially applaud the new provisions in sections 17E(1) and (2) which explicitly state that it is an offence of any person knowingly urging, on the ground of religion or religious belief or activity, the use of force or violence and the target group or target person is distinguished by religion or religious belief or activity, or by ethnicity, descent, nationality, language or political opinion, or any other characteristic whether or not of a similar kind.

sections.label: Protecting vulnerable groups from hate speech
sections.summary: Target groups may include atheists, racial communities, sexual orientations, nationalities or descents, and the provisions protect vulnerable groups including the LGBTQ community from hate speech and institutionalised discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The target group may be made up of atheists, individuals from a specific racial community, who share a similar sexual orientation, or have a certain nationality or descent like foreign workers or new citizens." In April 2019, the Minister for Home Affairs said that hate speech dehumanises marginalised groups, which enables individuals to justify violence against them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These new provisions serve to protect our vulnerable groups, including the LGBTQ community, from hate speech and institutionalised discrimination which, to my mind, always constitutes violence.

sections.label: Clarification on section 17E offence
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to clarify, as an illustration for the Bill, that the man's action could be an offence under sections 17E(1) and (2).

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would the Minister clarify, as an illustration for the Bill, that the man’s action could be an offence under the new provisions of section 17E(1) and (2)?

sections.label: Minister's expanded RO powers
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Minister make an RO without giving 14 days' notice to the person or religious group implicated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Instead, the Bill allows for the expanded powers of the Minister in being able to make an RO without 14 days’ notice of his intention to the person against whom the Order is made or to the religious group that is implicated.

sections.label: Appeals and negative attention
sections.summary: Affected parties may appeal within 14 days, but the RO would draw negative public attention to the religion affected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While affected parties can appeal within 14 days of the order, the RO having been made would cast negative public attention on the particular religion affected.

sections.label: Hearing affected parties before decisions
sections.summary: The speaker says hearing the affected person or group would aid decision-making and urges the Minister to clarify removing the notice period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hearing the affected person or religious group’s side of the story, such as on how the sources and necessity of these donations are, and the nature of contributions of the governing body members, would be extremely useful in decision-making.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I strongly urge the Minister to clarify on the removal of the notice period and the non-requirement of notice or consult.

sections.label: Stephen's Code for reasonable speech
sections.summary: The speaker calls Section 17F(10) implicit yet limiting and urges including a Stephen's Code like Canada and New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 17F(10) in the Bill is implicit yet limiting in this regard.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to consider the inclusion of a "Stephen’s Code" into our laws to provide protection for reasonable speech made with good intentions for the sake of protecting public interest like Canada and New Zealand have.

sections.label: Singapore's religious diversity and non-religious
sections.summary: Singapore is the world's most religiously diverse country, yet one in four Singaporeans follow no religion, per a 2019 survey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Singapore is the world’s most religiously diverse country.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, one in four Singaporeans do not follow a religion, according to the 2019 survey by the Institute for Policy Studies.

sections.label: Using interbelief instead of interfaith
sections.summary: The speaker urges using "interbelief" instead of "interfaith" so non-religious Singaporeans are not alienated, and asks interfaith communities to do the same.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: People of faith must know and understand that fellow Singaporeans who do not have a religion do not necessarily oppose religion, they simply hold a different set of beliefs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider using "interbelief" instead of "interfaith" in our official narrative so that we are not alienating 25% of our Singaporeans and for all interfaith communities to do the same.

sections.label: Mosque practices aligned with MRHA
sections.summary: MUIS mosque and religious institution practices already align with MRHA amendments on local leadership and foreign funding rules.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The practices in our mosques and religious institutions under MUIS are already aligned to the enhanced safeguards in the MRHA amendments, in particular, to ensure local leadership in our religious institutions, as well as regulations on foreign funding.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, all members of the MUIS Council and the board members of our madrasahs, are Singapore Citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are also proud that the strong support of the Muslim community in Singapore through the monthly contributions to the Mosque Building and MENDAKI Fund (MBMF) has allowed us to raise funds from our community to build and upgrade mosques in all our estates and to support education in our madrasahs without the need for foreign funding.

sections.label: Imam Nalla charged and repatriated
sections.summary: In 2017, Imam Nalla, a preacher from India, was charged and repatriated for remarks against Christians and Jews.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In 2017, Imam Nalla, a preacher from India, was charged and repatriated for making remarks against Christians and Jews.

sections.label: Registered asatizahs under ARS
sections.summary: Today, more than 4,500 asatizahs are registered under ARS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Today, we have more than 4,500 asatizahs registered under ARS.

sections.label: Murad Mohd Said struck off ARS
sections.summary: Murad Mohd Said was struck off ARS in May 2018 for segregationist teachings contravening the ARS Code of Ethics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For example, Murad Mohd Said, who was placed on a Restriction Order in December 2018, was struck off ARS earlier in May 2018 for his segregationist teachings that contravened the ARS Code of Ethics.

sections.label: Returning graduates must undergo PCICS
sections.summary: Starting next year, all returning religious graduates from overseas Islamic universities must undergo the PCICS programme to register under ARS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To enhance further, starting next year, all returning religious graduates from overseas Islamic universities must also undergo the Postgraduate Certificate in Islam in Contemporary Societies (PCICS) programme to be registered under ARS.

sections.label: COFA to submit recommendations
sections.summary: COFA will submit its recommendations to the Government early next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: COFA will submit its recommendations to the Government early next year.

sections.label: Commitment to Safeguard Religious Harmony
sections.summary: Religious leaders of different faiths developed the Commitment to Safeguard Religious Harmony, launched at the International Conference on Cohesive Societies in June this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The religious leaders of the different faiths mooted and developed the Commitment to Safeguard Religious Harmony that was launched during the International Conference on Cohesive Societies in June this year.

sections.label: Asatizah Recognition Scheme support
sections.summary: ARS began as a voluntary scheme in 2005, community and religious leaders asked in 2016 for it to be mandatory, and over 4,500 asatizahs are now registered.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: ARS was introduced as a voluntary scheme in 2005 and received strong support from the community, including amongst the asatizahs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This strong support was clearly displayed in 2016, when community and religious leaders themselves asked for ARS to be made mandatory.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Today, we have more than 4,500 asatizahs registered under ARS.

sections.label: Returning religious graduates PCICS requirement
sections.summary: From next year, all returning religious graduates from overseas Islamic universities must undergo the PCICS programme before registering under ARS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To enhance this further, starting next year, all returning religious graduates from overseas Islamic universities must also undergo the PCICS programme, before they can register under ARS.

sections.label: MRHA amendments and MUIS support
sections.summary: COFA will submit recommendations early next year, and MUIS, which was consulted on the MRHA amendments, supports them to protect religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: COFA will submit its recommendations to the Government early next year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Muslims and non-Muslims in Singapore have shown our region and the world that it is possible to have a model anchored in harmony, peaceful co-existence and honest, genuine relationships among the leaders and followers of different faiths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Hence, we believe that, as the global socio-religious landscape continues to evolve, the amendments to MRHA will ensure it remains an effective legal safeguard to protect religious harmony and bolsters the community’s ongoing efforts to strengthen our social cohesion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: MUIS has been consulted on the specific amendments to MRHA, and MUIS supports the amendments.

sections.label: MRHA introduction and enactment
sections.summary: The MRHA was introduced in 1990 and enacted in 1992, and this Act has never been used or amended.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some of the existing pieces of legislation include the MRHA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This Act was introduced in 1990 and enacted in 1992.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Second, to ensure that religion does not influence national politics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This Act has actually never been used or amended.

sections.label: Strengthening MRHA
sections.summary: MRHA needs to be strengthened so the country's well-being and interests continue to be protected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: MRHA needs to be strengthened so that we can continue to ensure the country's well-being and interests are protected.

sections.label: Incitement of enmity and ill-will
sections.summary: The passage says incitement of enmity, hatred or ill-will, even in private, could be a cause for concern.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Further, I appreciate that believers of a certain faith would have views on non-believers and any articulation of that may be perceived as offensive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: However, the fact that there had been an incitement of enmity, hatred or ill-will, even if it is in a private setting, could be a cause for concern.

sections.label: CRI introduction and non-mandatory process
sections.summary: The CRI offers a chance to edify, clarify and rebuild relations, and the process is not mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The CRI presents that opportunity to edify, clarify and rebuild relations and I am happy that it is being introduced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note though that the process is not mandatory.

sections.label: Legal measures and community engagements
sections.summary: The passage states legal measures and community engagements protect the multiracial and multi-religious community, and ROs will take immediate effect instead of 14 days' notice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: These efforts augment the legal framework that we put in place to preserve and protect our social fabric.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have faith that with the appropriate combination of legal measures as well as community engagements, and a conscious effort to consistently and vigorously protect the interests of our multiracial and multi-religious community, we would be able to maintain our harmony.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our policies have been carefully reviewed and updated over the years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This round, as usual, we are not taking things for granted and will be introducing ROs which will take immediate effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is a significant change, compared to the current 14 days' notice.

sections.label: Filtering feedback and online enforcement
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will filter feedback, conduct online checks, use technology like AI, and enforce ROs against online service providers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry share how it will filter feedback, conduct online checks and whether it will utilise technology, such as artificial intelligence (AI)?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: After identifying online threats, how could we enforce our ROs against online service providers to remove such provocative posts immediately to prevent them from being circulated in Singapore?

sections.label: Special mediation team for disputes
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a special mediation team will be considered to resolve disputes sensitively and fairly, noting Singapore's religious diversity ranking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry consider having a special mediation team to help resolve such disputes and to ensure that these cases can be handled sensitively and fairly?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Singapore is ranked as the most religiously diverse nation in the world by the Pew Research Centre.

sections.label: Inadequacy of 14-day notice
sections.summary: The passage states the current 14-day notice before an order takes effect is inadequate in the current environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The current 14-day notice before the order can take effect is inadequate in our current environment.

sections.label: CRI prosecution risk and foreign influence safeguards
sections.summary: A Member asks about offenders insincerely undergoing CRI to avoid prosecution, and notes safeguards requiring religious organisations to reserve key positions for Singaporeans or PRs with case-by-case exemptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I have another concern which I seek clarification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is stated that if the offender completes CRI, criminal prosecution cannot be taken against him.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What is the risk of offenders choosing to undergo CRI, going through the motions without any sincere intention, in order to avoid criminal prosecutions?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: One of the safeguards against foreign influence is to require religious organisations to only open key positions to Singaporeans or PRs, with "exemptions granted on a case-by-case basis".

sections.label: Government information push for religious harmony
sections.summary: The Government must push key information to the public sustainably so citizens and residents gain basic discernment and knowledge, setting a firm foundation for religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For this reason, the Government must take on the task of pushing out key nuggets of information to the public, including young and old, on a sustainable basis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It is very important that citizens and residents attain at least a basic level of discernment and knowledge so that our community's foundation for religious harmony is firmly set.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In addition, with mutual respect, tolerance and a gracious attitude, we will be able to enjoy the fruits of a harmonious and vibrant society for years to come.

sections.label: Act's two main objectives
sections.summary: The Act had two objectives: guiding followers of different religions to exercise moderation and tolerance and not instigate religious enmity or hatred, and keeping religion and politics separate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Act had two main objectives: firstly, to guide followers of different religions to exercise moderation and tolerance towards one another and their beliefs and not to instigate religious enmity or hatred; and, secondly, for religion and politics to be kept separate.

sections.label: Facebook admission on Sri Lanka post
sections.summary: At a London hearing on 27 November 2018, a Facebook executive admitted the company made a mistake in not removing a post that incited racial and religious hatred and violence in Sri Lanka.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At an international hearing on fake news and disinformation in London on 27 November 2018, a Facebook executive admitted, in response to a question by Senior Minister of State Edwin Tong, that the company "made a mistake" in not removing a post that incited racial and religious hatred and violence in Sri Lanka and caused people to lose their lives.

sections.label: Welcoming immediate RO effect
sections.summary: A Member welcomes the move for the RO to take immediate effect before the offensive statement spreads like wildfire and causes irreversible damage to social fabric and communal bonds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We, Singaporeans, know full well the effects of forest fires.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I welcome the move for the RO to take immediate effect before the offensive statement starts spreading like wildfire and causing irreversible damage to our social fabric and communal bonds.

sections.label: How CRI will be administered
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister how CRI will be administered practically and what sort of activities the Ministry has in mind for carrying out CRI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how CRI will be administered practically and, more specifically, what sort of activities does the Ministry have in mind in carrying out CRI?

sections.label: Foreign influence and religious bodies
sections.summary: PM Lee warned in New York about weaponisation of religion, and foreign money was said to be routed through local foundations and religious bodies to fund political campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just last month, Prime Minister Lee spoke in New York at the Appeal of Conscience Foundation Annual Awards Dinner where he warned about weaponisation of religion as a growing phenomenon in countries around the world where foreign actors influence and/or interfere in local religious organisations to exploit religious fault lines, cause social upheavals, and create political instability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In one of my discussions, it was shared that in the years leading up to the general elections, huge amounts of money from foreign sources were routed through local foundations and religious bodies to fund political campaigns and their agendas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We cannot allow religious bodies to be manipulated in the same fashion, and the need to mitigate foreign influence is a necessary amendment to the Bill.

sections.label: Foreign donations to non-registered religious groups
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry's stand on foreign donations to non-registered local religious groups affiliated with international organisations, and says amendments require greater transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, Mr Speaker, what is the Ministry’s view and stand on foreign donations received by non-registered local religious groups affiliated with international religious organisations, in particular, those operating under the banner of private enterprises or social organisations in the form of educational establishments, training agencies, meditation centres or any such other entities?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe that the amendments will not affect the work of religious organisations in Singapore, but it will certainly require greater transparency from them in terms of whom they are getting their funds from, who are their leaders, and whom they are affiliated to internationally.

sections.label: Maintenance of Religious Harmony law unused
sections.summary: In the past 30 years, there was no need to use the Maintenance of Religious Harmony law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the past 30 years, we did not have the need to use this Maintenance of Religious Harmony law.

sections.label: Bill on foreign actors and religious harmony
sections.summary: The Bill imposes citizenship or permanent residence requirements on religious organisation leadership and disclosure of large donations, and allows restrictions on foreign donors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to prevent foreign actors from adversely affecting religious harmony in Singapore by imposing requirements relating to citizenship or permanent residence requirements on the leadership of religious organisations and the disclosure of large donations, amongst others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: An RO can also be issued to prohibit a religious organisation from receiving donations from specific or all foreign donors, to require the entire governing body to be Singapore Citizens and to require specific foreigners to be suspended or removed from office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Earlier this year, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary shared that 24 radicalised Singaporeans have been dealt with under the ISA since 2015.

sections.label: Disclosure of foreign donations
sections.summary: The speaker supports requiring religious organisations to disclose foreign donations of $10,000 or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, I support the requirement for religious organisations to disclose "foreign donations" of $10,000 or more.

sections.label: CRI as reconciliatory approach
sections.summary: Section 16H provides for CRI as a reconciliatory approach for addressing offending behaviour that has wounded a religious community's feelings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, section 16H provides for CRI as a reconciliatory approach for addressing offending behaviour that has wounded the feelings of a religious community.

sections.label: CSO limits for new offences
sections.summary: A CSO cannot be imposed for offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding three years, such as inciting hatred and urging violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A CSO may not be a sentencing option for some of the new offences in this Bill because a CSO cannot be imposed for an offence which is punishable with a term of imprisonment which exceeds three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The offence of inciting hatred and ill-will is punishable with imprisonment of five years, while the offence of urging violence on religious grounds or against religious groups is punishable with imprisonment of up to 10 years.

sections.label: CRI after trial commencement
sections.summary: Under section 16H(5)(b), a CRI cannot be entered into after trial commencement, and the Minister is asked to consider extending it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yet, under section 16H(5)(b), a CRI cannot be entered into after the commencement of trial.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider extending CRI as a sentencing option?

sections.label: Act never invoked in 30 years
sections.summary: Press coverage before the Second Reading often highlighted that the Act has never been invoked since it came into effect nearly 30 years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the press coverage leading up to the Second Reading of the Bill, it has been often highlighted that the Act has never once been invoked since it came into effect nearly 30 years ago.

sections.label: Review of MRHA
sections.summary: After almost 30 years, the MRHA is reviewed to address social media, foreign interference, and consolidate criminal provisions previously under the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It helps to maintain law and order, without which no religious beliefs could be upheld or practised in peace." After almost 30 years, it is timely to review the MRHA to ensure that it is strengthened to deal with evolving issues that potentially have an impact on the maintenance of religious harmony in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note that the principal aim of the amendment Bill is to deal with the challenge of social media which can cause a viralling and deleterious effect on our society very quickly, and possible foreign interference in local religious organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It also consolidates all the criminal provisions dealing with religious harmony, previously under the Penal Code, under MRHA.

sections.label: Removal of RO notice requirement
sections.summary: The requirement that the Minister may issue an RO only after notice and a 14-day representation period is removed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
